newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Creditanstalt preferred slump in early trading.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt preferred slump in early trading.

text.p: Preferred shares of Creditanstalt were down more than five percent in early Vienna trade on Thursday as uncertainty over the share's fate after the acquisition of the bank by rival Bank Austria persisted.
At 0855 GMT, the shares were down 25 schillings at 436, just up from an earlier low of 428. The ATX index of 21 blue chips was down 0.57 percent at 1,162.71 at the same time.
"Nobody knows what'll happen with the preferred shares," said one trader.

Bank Austria has acquired the state's 70 percent ordinary voting stake in the bank and offered small holders of ordinary shares to buy them out, but has kept mum about its plans for holders of preferred stock.
Traders said the preference shares could fall to as low as 400 schillings before rebounding. "I really wouldn't want to rule that out," said one.
The shares have shed some 12 percent since the Bank Austria-Creditanstalt deal was announced over the weekend.
